To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we can identify CENTRAL PROPOSITION FACETS of an argument from human summaries of dialog, we can recognize that two FACETS are similar, and we can predict the FACET similarity with a.54 accuracy score.

1) we can identify the CENTRAL PROPOSALS of online dialogs by analyzing human summaries of the dialogs; 2) we can group CENTRAL PROPOSAL into FACETS by comparing their similarity to each other; and 3) we can automatically identify FACETS with a correlation score of.54, which is higher than a baseline of.39 using n-grams and.45 using semantic textual similarity.

1) we can use human summaries to identify the most central propositions of an argument; 2) we can group these into FACETS; and 3) we can automatically predict the similarity of FACETS between different discussions.
